title: ISRO Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)
sources: ISRO mission pages for the Mars Orbiter Mission

verified.text: The Mars Orbiter Mission, also called Mangalyaan, was launched by ISRO on 5 November 2013 on a PSLV rocket from Sriharikota.
It entered orbit around Mars on 24 September 2014.
India became the first country to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt, and the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit.
The mission cost about ₹450 crore, roughly 74 million US dollars (in Hindi: लगभग 7.4 करोड़ डॉलर).
That was less than the reported budget of the Hollywood film Gravity, about 100 million US dollars (in Hindi: लगभग 10 करोड़ डॉलर).
The spacecraft first circled Earth for about a month, raising its orbit step by step, before leaving for Mars on 1 December 2013.
The journey to Mars took about 300 days (298 days).
Designed to last six months, the orbiter worked for about eight years, until contact was lost in 2022.
ISRO, the Indian Space Research Organisation, is headquartered in Bengaluru.

knownErrors.correction: It was an orbiter: it circled Mars, it never landed.
Launched 5 November 2013; reached Mars orbit 24 September 2014.
Gravity cost about 100 million US dollars (roughly ₹600+ crore at the time); Mangalyaan cost about ₹450 crore (about 74 million dollars).
74 million US dollars = about 7.4 crore dollars (₹450 crore).
